newsitem.title: GREECE: Attica Enterprises says Jan-Apr turnover up 20pct.
newsitem.headline: Attica Enterprises says Jan-Apr turnover up 20pct.

text.p: Greek shipper Attica Enterprises said in a statement that its consolidated turnover rose 20 percent to 3.9 billion drachmas in the first four months of 1997 from 3.2 billion in the same period in 1996.
Its Superfast II and II passenger and vehicle ferries, serving the sea route between Greece and Italy, increased their market share in passenger, truck and private cars and campers traffic, it added.

Attica's market share in passenger traffic rose to 56.4 percent in the period January-April 1997 from 48.6 percent in the same period in 1996, truck traffic to 45.9 percent from 38.7 percent and cars and campers to 59.7 percent from 44.4 perent, it said.

The construction of its two new modern car passenger ferries, representing an investment of about $200 million, was at an advanced stage at Kvaerner Masa-Yards in Finland and would be ready for delivery in the first quarter of 1998, it said.
The Athens bourse approved Attica's 8.15 billion drachma rights issue in early May.
The company will issue 5,256,000 new common bearer shares at 1,550 drachmas. The terms will be one new share per five outstanding.

Attica Enterprises will use 70 percent of the proceeds to raise the share capital of is wholly-owned subsidiary Superfast Ferries Maritime SA with an eye to finance current and future buildings of ships.
The remainder will be used for working capital needs. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
